# More than Music with MIDI

<!-- Devices send signals. Your sketch decides what they mean. -->

Processing Community Day 2026 · New York · October 3 · George Mandis

---

## 1. MIDI is older than you think

---

### 1983

<p class="fragment">Say "MIDI" and people hear canyon.mid</p>

<p class="fragment">That's General MIDI, a 1991 sound bank. Different thing.</p>

<p class="fragment">1983: Roland, Sequential, Yamaha and Korg agree on how synths talk</p>

<p class="fragment">43 years old. Every OS already speaks it.</p>

<p class="fragment"><strong>Processing speaks it too. Nothing to install.</strong></p>

---

## 2. The whole protocol is three bytes

---

### [144, 60, 127]

<!-- visual: bytes -->

| Byte | Job |
| --- | --- |
| 144 | status: what happened, and on which channel |
| 60 | data: which one |
| 127 | data: how much |

<p class="fragment">Data bytes are always <strong>0 to 127</strong></p>

<p class="fragment">You'll see these numbers in ten minutes</p>

---

### What the standard says they mean

<!-- visual: bytes -->

<p class="fragment">144 → note on, channel 1</p>

<p class="fragment">60 → middle C</p>

<p class="fragment">127 → as hard as you can hit it</p>

<p class="fragment">Like HTTP codes. 404 means Not Found because everyone agreed.</p>

---

### 418

<!-- visual: teapot -->

I'm a teapot.

---

### The standard is a suggestion

<p class="fragment">Button → note on, note off</p>

<p class="fragment">Knob, joystick, sensor → control change, 0 to 127</p>

<p class="fragment"><strong>Your sketch decides what 60 means.</strong></p>

<p class="fragment">Draw a circle. Or open the garage door.</p>

---

## 3. Things that have been MIDI

---

### Bananas

<!-- visual: bananas -->

![Three bananas wired to a Circuit Playground](img/midi-bananas.jpg)

<p class="fragment">Clip on each banana. Touch one, note on.</p>

<p class="fragment">A banana is mostly water, so the touch pad doesn't care</p>

<p class="fragment">Processing sees 144, 60, 127. Same as a piano key.</p>

<p class="fragment"><strong>Nothing in the chain knows there's a banana</strong></p>

---

### 2019: a pile of Circuit Playgrounds

*A coin-sized board glowing green next to a laptop*

<p class="fragment">Buttons, a switch, an accelerometer, light, sound, temperature, touch pads, ten NeoPixels</p>

<p class="fragment">My firmware: ten modes, shows up as a MIDI device</p>

<p class="fragment"><strong>The same boards are on this table</strong></p>

| useMIDI PipSqueak | lots | joystick + one button |
| Circuit Playground Express | about 10 | sensors in, 10 pixels out |

### Step one: plug in and look

<p class="fragment">The Explorer is a Processing sketch</p>

<p class="fragment">Lists every device, decodes every message</p>

<p class="fragment"><code>PipSqueak · CC 1 · ch 1 · 97 · [176, 1, 97]</code></p>

<p class="fragment">Draws the device when it knows it</p>

<p class="fragment">Send panel, so you can light things up</p>

<p class="fragment"><strong>Plug in any device!</strong> Learn how your instrument is talking to you</p>

---

### Five minutes to pixels

<p class="fragment">Open Processing (or start a p5 sketch)</p>

<p class="fragment">Open the starter sketch for your device (if you want)</p>

<p class="fragment">Run it. Wiggle the thing.</p>

<p class="fragment">Change the line that says <code>// change this</code></p>

<p class="fragment">Then 50 minutes to build. I'll come around. <strong>Show and tell at the end.</strong></p>
